metadata.title: EXIF Viewer
metadata.description: View EXIF metadata of images

faqs.question: What is EXIF data?
faqs.answer: EXIF (Exchangeable Image File Format) is metadata stored in image files. It includes camera model, settings (aperture, shutter speed, ISO), date taken, GPS coordinates, and more.

faqs.question: How do I view EXIF data?
faqs.answer: Drag and drop an image onto the upload area, or click to select a file. The tool extracts and displays all available EXIF data, including camera information, settings, and location data.

faqs.question: Do all images have EXIF data?
faqs.answer: No. EXIF data is typically added by digital cameras and smartphones. Images downloaded from the web or edited may have no EXIF data. Some formats (like PNG) don't support EXIF.

faqs.question: Does EXIF data include GPS location?
faqs.answer: It can. Many smartphones store GPS coordinates in EXIF data if camera location permissions are enabled on your device. You can view location data with this tool.

faqs.question: Can I remove EXIF data?
faqs.answer: This tool only views EXIF data, it doesn't remove it. To strip EXIF data, use a dedicated image editor or privacy tool.

faqs.question: Are images sent to a server?
faqs.answer: No. All EXIF extraction happens locally in your browser. Images are never uploaded to any server.

labels.hint: Choose a JPEG image to view its metadata.

faqs.question: What are historical market returns?
faqs.answer: The US stock market has historically averaged about 10% annually (nominal), or 7% after inflation. Bonds average 5-6%. These are long-term averages - individual years vary widely.

faqs.question: How do fees affect investment returns?
faqs.answer: Fees directly reduce returns. A 1% fee reduces your final balance by about 25% over 30 years. Low-fee index funds at 0.1% outperform actively managed funds charging 1%+ after fees.

faqs.question: How often should I rebalance?
faqs.answer: Annually, or when allocations drift more than 5% from target. Rebalancing maintains risk levels and enforces "buy low, sell high". Rebalancing too often triggers taxes and trading costs.

faqs.question: How do taxes affect returns?
faqs.answer: Taxes significantly reduce net returns. In taxable accounts, capital gains and dividends are taxed annually. Use tax-advantaged accounts (401k, IRA) for long-term investing to defer or avoid taxes.

faqs.answer: Paste JSON into the input field. The tool immediately checks the syntax and shows whether it's valid. If there are errors, it shows the exact location and cause.

faqs.answer: Common errors include missing commas, trailing commas, single quotes instead of double quotes, missing quotes, unclosed brackets, and invalid escape characters. The tool highlights the exact issue.

faqs.question: How is the monthly payment calculated?
faqs.answer: The calculator uses the standard amortization formula: M = P[r(1+r)^n]/[(1+r)^n-1], where P is the loan amount, r is the monthly interest rate, and n is the total number of payments.

faqs.question: What types of loans does this work for?
faqs.answer: This calculator works for any fixed-rate loan with equal monthly payments - personal loans, auto loans, student loans, home equity loans, and more. It doesn't apply to variable-rate or interest-only loans.

faqs.question: How does the loan term affect total cost?
faqs.answer: Longer terms mean lower monthly payments but significantly more total interest paid. Shorter terms have higher payments but save money overall. Always compare total cost, not just the monthly payment.

metadata.title: Mortgage Calculator
metadata.description: Calculate monthly payments, taxes, insurance, PMI, and amortization schedule.

faqs.question: How is the monthly mortgage payment calculated?
faqs.answer: The monthly payment is calculated using the standard amortization formula: M = P[r(1+r)^n]/[(1+r)^n - 1], where P is the loan amount, r is the monthly interest rate, and n is the total number of payments.

faqs.question: How accurate are the property tax and insurance estimates?
faqs.answer: Property tax rates are based on effective rates by state. Insurance rates are based on average annual premiums by state. Both are applied as a percentage of the home price and update automatically when you change state or price. These are state averages; actual costs vary by county, city, coverage level, and property specifics.

faqs.question: What is PMI?
faqs.answer: Private mortgage insurance (PMI) is required when your down payment is less than 20% of the home price. It typically costs 0.3%-1.5% of the loan amount per year and protects the lender in case of default.

faqs.question: Why do property taxes differ so much by state?
faqs.answer: Property tax rates range from 0.28% in Hawaii to 2.47% in New Jersey. That means on a $350,000 home you'd pay $980 per year in Hawaii and $8,645 in New Jersey. States without income tax typically have higher property taxes to compensate.

faqs.question: Why is home insurance so expensive in some states?
faqs.answer: Insurance costs are significantly higher in states prone to natural disasters. Florida averages about 1.05% of home value due to hurricane risk. Oklahoma and Louisiana are high due to tornado and hurricane exposure. Hawaii, Utah, and Oregon have the lowest rates.

faqs.question: Does this include taxes and insurance?
faqs.answer: Yes. After you select a state, property taxes and home insurance are estimated automatically based on state averages and the home price. These are added to the principal and interest payment to show the true monthly cost. You can also adjust both values manually.

faqs.question: What is an amortization schedule?
faqs.answer: An amortization schedule shows how each monthly payment is split between principal and interest over the life of the loan. Early payments are mostly interest; later payments are mostly principal.

faqs.question: What is an Open Graph preview?
faqs.answer: An Open Graph preview shows how your website looks when shared on Facebook, LinkedIn, and other social platforms. It uses your site's og: meta tags to display the title, description, image, and URL.

faqs.question: How do I use the OG preview?
faqs.answer: Enter your website URL. The tool fetches and parses the Open Graph tags, then shows previews of how it will look when shared on Facebook and Twitter.

faqs.question: Why does my preview look wrong?
faqs.answer: Check that your site has the correct og:title, og:description, og:image, and og:url tags. Images should be at least 1200x630 pixels. Some platforms cache previews, so it may take time to update.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Facebook and Twitter previews?
faqs.answer: Facebook uses Open Graph tags, while Twitter uses Twitter Card tags (falling back to Open Graph if available). The layouts and designs are also slightly different.

faqs.question: Can I preview the OG tags of a specific page?
faqs.answer: Yes. Enter any URL and the tool will fetch that page's OG tags and display the preview.

faqs.question: Are the previews accurate?
faqs.answer: Previews are based on the OG tags fetched from your website. They aim to match Facebook's and Twitter's current designs, but actual rendering may differ slightly due to platform updates.

faqs.question: How do I calculate a percentage of a number?
faqs.answer: Multiply the number by the percentage divided by 100. For example, 25% of 200 = 200 * (25/100) = 50.

faqs.question: How do I calculate percentage change?
faqs.answer: Percentage change = ((new value - old value) / old value) * 100. A change from 80 to 100 is ((100-80)/80) * 100 = a 25% increase.

faqs.question: What's the difference between percentage and percentage points?
faqs.answer: A change from 10% to 15% is a 5 percentage point increase, but a 50% percentage increase. Percentage points measure absolute differences; percentages measure relative change.

faqs.question: What is the 4% rule?
faqs.answer: The 4% rule suggests you can withdraw 4% of your retirement savings per year without running out of money over 30 years. It's based on research using historical market returns. Adjust for inflation to maintain purchasing power.

faqs.question: How much do I need to retire?
faqs.answer: Multiply your annual expenses by 25 (based on the 4% rule). If you need $50,000 per year, aim for $1.25 million. This includes Social Security and pensions as income sources.

faqs.question: How does Social Security affect retirement?
faqs.answer: Social Security replaces about 40% of pre-retirement income. Higher earners get a lower replacement percentage. Claim at 67 (full retirement age), or wait until 70 to increase payments by 8%/year.

faqs.question: How aggressive should I invest?
faqs.answer: A rule of thumb: stock percentage = 110 - your age. At 30: 80% stocks. At 60: 50% stocks. Reduce risk as you approach retirement. But adjust based on your risk tolerance and time horizon.

faqs.question: How do I convert annual salary to hourly?
faqs.answer: Divide the annual salary by the number of hours worked per year. For a standard 40-hour work week, 52 weeks: $65,000 / 2,080 hours = $31.25/hour.

faqs.question: How do I convert hourly to annual salary?
faqs.answer: Multiply the hourly rate by the hours per week, then by the weeks per year. $20/hour * 40 hours * 52 weeks = $41,600/year.

faqs.question: Are the tax estimates accurate?
faqs.answer: Tax estimates use a simplified 2026 US federal tax bracket for single filers with the standard deduction, plus FICA (7.65%). Actual taxes vary based on filing status, state taxes, deductions, and credits. Use as a rough guide only.

faqs.question: What if I have paid vacation?
faqs.answer: If your employer provides paid vacation, keep weeks per year at 52 - you still get paid for those weeks. Only reduce the number if you have unpaid time off.

faqs.question: How does compound interest affect savings?
faqs.answer: Compound interest accrues on both your principal and accumulated interest. Compounding monthly vs. annually produces slightly higher returns. The difference grows with time and rate.

faqs.question: How do regular deposits affect growth?
faqs.answer: Regular deposits significantly increase the final balance through compounding. Depositing $200/month at a 5% annual return for 10 years = about $31,000 - you contribute $24,000 and interest contributes $7,000.

faqs.question: What's the difference between savings and money market accounts?
faqs.answer: Savings accounts offer a fixed rate and simple access. Money market accounts typically offer higher rates but require higher minimum balances and may offer check-writing privileges. Both are FDIC-insured.

faqs.question: How does inflation affect my savings?
faqs.answer: Inflation erodes purchasing power. 3% inflation reduces purchasing power by 26% over 10 years. Always compare your savings rate to inflation - if the rate is below inflation, your money is losing real value.

faqs.question: Should I tip on the pre-tax or after-tax amount?
faqs.answer: Traditionally, tips are calculated on the pre-tax subtotal. However, many people calculate on the total including tax for simplicity. The difference is usually small.

faqs.question: Is this URL shortener free?
faqs.answer: Completely free. Short links are created through the public APIs of is.gd and TinyURL, with no account, signup, or payment required.

faqs.question: Can I choose a custom short link?
faqs.answer: Yes. Enter an alias in the optional custom field and the tool will request that short code from is.gd. Whether the custom code is available depends on the provider's service status and usage limits.

faqs.question: Are my links tracked or logged?
faqs.answer: No. The tool only forwards your URL to the shortening service and returns the short link. This site performs no statistics, tracking, or storage.

faqs.question: Do short links expire?
faqs.answer: Links generated by is.gd and TinyURL are permanent and don't expire, unless the target page is removed.

faqs.question: Why was my short link generated by TinyURL?
faqs.answer: The tool prefers is.gd (which supports structured errors and custom short links). When is.gd is rate-limited or unavailable, it automatically falls back to TinyURL so you still get a working short link.

faqs.question: What URLs are supported?
faqs.answer: Any public http or https link. Private addresses or localhost will be rejected by the shortening services.

faqs.question: Why doesn't my short link open?
faqs.answer: Short links are hosted by third-party services is.gd and TinyURL, and these domains may not be accessible from some networks (such as mainland China). The short link itself is valid—if it doesn't open, switch to a network that can reach these domains.

metadata.title: URL Slug Generator
metadata.description: Generate URL-friendly slugs from text

faqs.question: What is a URL slug?
faqs.answer: A URL slug is the text portion of a URL that identifies a specific page. It should be readable, SEO-friendly, and contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. For example: "my-blog-post".

faqs.question: How do I generate a slug?
faqs.answer: Type or paste text into the input field. The tool automatically converts it into a URL-friendly slug, removing special characters, converting to lowercase, and replacing spaces with hyphens.

faqs.question: Are slugs important for SEO?
faqs.answer: Yes. Descriptive slugs help search engines understand page content. They also make it easier for users to predict what a link contains. Good slugs can improve search engine rankings and click-through rates.

faqs.question: What characters should I use in a slug?
faqs.answer: Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. Avoid spaces, uppercase, special characters, and consecutive hyphens. Keep slugs short but descriptive.

faqs.question: Can I customize the slug?
faqs.answer: Yes. After the initial slug is generated, you can edit it manually for further customization. The tool provides a clean starting point.

faqs.question: Is the slug generator safe?
faqs.answer: Yes. This tool generates slugs locally in your browser. No data is sent to any server.

intro.title: What is a URL Slug Generator?
paragraphs: A URL Slug Generator is a free online tool that creates URL-friendly slugs from text. It converts text to lowercase, removes special characters, and replaces spaces with hyphens. All conversion happens in your browser.

sections.title: How to Generate a Slug
paragraphs: Type or paste text into the input field. The tool automatically converts it into a URL-friendly slug. Copy the result for use in URLs.

sections.title: Slug Best Practices
paragraphs: Keep slugs short but descriptive. Use keywords without stuffing them. Avoid stop words (like a, the, is) unless essential to meaning. Use hyphens to separate words.

faqs.question: How much should I contribute to my 401(k)?
faqs.answer: At minimum, contribute enough to get the full employer match - that's free money. The 2026 contribution limit is $23,500 ($31,000 if 50 or older). Financial advisors often recommend saving 15% of your income for retirement.

faqs.question: What is an employer match?
faqs.answer: Many employers match a percentage of your 401(k) contributions. A common match is 50% of contributions up to 6% of your salary. On a $75,000 salary, that's $2,250 per year in free money.

faqs.question: What return rate should I use?
faqs.answer: The S&P 500 has averaged about 10% per year, or about 7% after inflation. Use 7% for a realistic inflation-adjusted estimate, or 10% for a nominal return estimate. Be conservative when planning.

faqs.question: How do I calculate my age?
faqs.answer: Age = Current Date - Birth Date. The calculator computes full years, months, and days. For example, born May 15, 1990, and today May 15, 2024 = 34 years old.

faqs.question: Why might my age differ in different countries?
faqs.answer: Age calculation is universal, but cultural interpretations can differ. Some cultures use nominal age (1 year old at birth), while others use zero age (0 at birth). This calculator uses the international standard.

faqs.question: How do I calculate days between two dates?
faqs.answer: Days = End Date - Start Date. The calculator accounts for leap years. For example, January 1, 2024 to December 31, 2024 = 365 days (2024 is a leap year).

metadata.title: Amortization Calculator

faqs.question: What is amortization?
faqs.answer: Amortization is spreading a loan into a series of fixed payments. Early payments are mostly interest; later payments are mostly principal. The amortization schedule shows this breakdown for each payment.

faqs.question: How do extra payments help?
faqs.answer: Extra payments go directly toward the principal, reducing the balance faster. On a $250,000 mortgage at 6.5% over 30 years, adding just $200 per month saves about $108,000 in interest and pays off the loan 7 years early.

faqs.question: Why do my early payments go mostly to interest?
faqs.answer: Interest is calculated on the remaining balance. Early on, the balance is large, so most of your payment goes toward interest. As the balance shrinks, more goes toward principal. This is normal for amortized loans.

metadata.title: Body Fat Calculator
metadata.description: Estimate your body fat percentage using the U.S. Navy formula from waist, neck, and hip measurements.

faqs.question: How does the U.S. Navy method work?
faqs.answer: The U.S. Navy body fat formula uses circumference measurements (waist, neck, and hips for women) combined with height to estimate body fat percentage. It is fairly accurate for most people and requires no specialized equipment.

faqs.question: How do I measure correctly?
faqs.answer: Waist: measure at the narrowest point (at navel level for men). Neck: measure below the larynx. Hips (women only): measure at the widest point. Use a soft tape measure, keep it snug but not compressed, and measure in the morning.

faqs.question: What is a healthy body fat percentage?
faqs.answer: Men: 10-20% is considered fit, 6-13% for athletes. Women: 18-28% is fit, 14-20% for athletes. Essential fat minimums are about 2-5% for men and 10-13% for women.

metadata.title: Budget Calculator
metadata.description: Plan a monthly budget by expense category and compare with the 50/30/20 rule.

faqs.question: What is the 50/30/20 rule?
faqs.answer: The 50/30/20 rule suggests: 50% to needs (housing, utilities, groceries), 30% to wants (entertainment, dining out), and 20% to savings and debt repayment. It's a starting point for a balanced budget.

faqs.question: How do I track expenses?
faqs.answer: Record every transaction for a month, use bank statements, or try a budgeting app. Categorize spending (housing, food, transportation). Identify areas of overspending and adjust.

faqs.question: How often should I review my budget?
faqs.answer: Review and adjust monthly. Life changes (new job, moving, a baby) need immediate updates. An annual review ensures your budget stays aligned with long-term goals.

faqs.question: What if my income is irregular?
faqs.answer: Use your lowest monthly income as the base. Allocate extra income to savings and debt. Build an emergency fund (3-6 months of expenses) for low-income months.

metadata.title: Calorie Calculator
metadata.description: Calculate your daily calorie needs based on age, gender, height, weight, and activity level.

faqs.question: How are daily calories calculated?
faqs.answer: This calculator uses the Mifflin-St Jeor equation to calculate your Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR), then multiplies it by an activity factor to get your Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE). The Mifflin-St Jeor equation is considered the most accurate equation for most people.

faqs.question: How many calories should I eat to lose weight?
faqs.answer: Reducing your daily intake by 500 calories leads to roughly 1 pound of weight loss per week. A 250-calorie reduction is about 0.5 pounds per week. Don't go below 1,200 calories for women or 1,500 calories for men without medical supervision.

faqs.question: What is the difference between BMR and TDEE?
faqs.answer: BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate) is the calories your body burns at complete rest - just to stay alive. TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) is BMR plus the calories burned through activity. TDEE is what you actually need to eat to maintain your weight.

faqs.question: Is the calorie calculator accurate?
faqs.answer: Calorie calculators provide estimates, not exact numbers. Individual metabolic differences range from +/- 10-15%. Use the result as a starting point, track your weight for 2-3 weeks, then adjust up or down based on actual results.

metadata.title: Concrete Calculator
metadata.description: Estimate concrete volume and the number of bags needed based on length, width, and depth.

faqs.question: How do I calculate how much concrete I need?
faqs.answer: Measure the length, width, and depth (thickness) of the project area. Multiply these three dimensions together to get the volume. For a rectangular slab, use length x width x depth. For a cylinder, use pi x radius squared x height. Always add 5-10% extra material for waste, spillage, and uneven subgrade.

faqs.question: How many bags of concrete do I need?
faqs.answer: First calculate the total cubic feet required. Then divide by the bag yield: a 40-lb bag covers 0.30 cubic feet, a 60-lb bag covers 0.45 cubic feet, and an 80-lb bag covers 0.60 cubic feet. For example, a 10x10 foot slab 4 inches thick needs about 33.3 cubic feet, about 56 bags of 80-lb concrete mix.

faqs.question: How thick should a concrete slab be?
faqs.answer: Sidewalks and patios typically require 4 inches of concrete. Driveways and garage floors should be 6 inches thick. Foundation walls are usually 8 inches, and foundations or footings are typically 12 inches thick. Heavier loads and vehicle traffic require thicker slabs.

faqs.question: What is the difference between cubic yards and cubic feet of concrete?
faqs.answer: 1 cubic yard equals 27 cubic feet. Ready-mix concrete bought from a truck is usually sold by the cubic yard, while bagged concrete is measured in cubic feet. To convert cubic feet to cubic yards, divide by 27. For example, 81 cubic feet equals 3 cubic yards.

faqs.question: How much does a yard of concrete cost?
faqs.answer: Ready-mix concrete typically costs $120 to $200 per cubic yard delivered, depending on your location, mix type, and delivery distance. Orders below 5-10 yards may incur a short-load fee. Specialty mixes, fiber reinforcement, or accelerated curing may add $10-30 per yard.

faqs.question: Should I add extra concrete for waste?
faqs.answer: Yes, always add a 5-10% waste factor to your calculated volume. This accounts for spillage, uneven subgrade, form irregularities, and over-excavation. For complex shapes like stairs or irregular forms, consider adding 10-15% extra. It's always better to have extra concrete than not enough during a pour.

faqs.question: When should I use bagged vs. ready-mix concrete?
faqs.answer: Bagged concrete is best for small projects under 1 cubic yard, such as setting fence posts, small pads, or repairs. For projects over 1-2 cubic yards, ready-mix delivery is more cost-effective and practical. Mixing more than 40-50 bags by hand is very labor-intensive.

whatIs.title: How to Use the Concrete Calculator
whatIs.content: This calculator helps you estimate the amount of concrete needed for any project. Choose the shape you're pouring, enter the dimensions, and get instant results in cubic yards, cubic feet, and cubic meters. You can add multiple sections to calculate combined totals for complex projects.

howTo.title: Supported Shapes
howTo.content: Slab/Square: for patios, sidewalks, driveways, and garage floors. Enter length, width, and depth. Cylinder/Column: for round columns, piers, sonotubes, and post holes. Enter diameter and height. Wall/Footing: for foundation walls, retaining walls, and footings. Enter length, height, and wall thickness. Stairs: for concrete steps. Enter the number of steps, riser height, tread width, and total stair width.

tips.title: Tips
tips.content: Always order 5-10% more concrete than your calculations to account for waste and uneven ground. For ready-mix deliveries, most companies have a 1 cubic yard minimum, and small orders may incur a short-load fee. One 80-lb bag of premix concrete yields about 0.6 cubic feet of cured concrete.
